source_caption:
The Princess Diaries introduced the world to a young Anne Hathaway and instantly turned her into a star. In her feature film debut, Hathaway plays Mia Thermopolis, an awkward and shy teenager who discovers that she’s the heir to the throne of a small European kingdom.

What made Anne Hathaway so perfect for the role was how naturally she balanced comedy, vulnerability, and charm. Mia feels like a real teenager: insecure, clumsy, and overwhelmed by the sudden changes in her life. As she slowly grows into her confidence, Hathaway makes the transformation feel genuine rather than simply physical.

Directed by Garry Marshall, the film became a beloved coming-of-age classic, thanks largely to the chemistry between Hathaway and Julie Andrews, who plays the elegant Queen Clarisse. Their relationship forms the emotional heart of the story, blending humor with heartfelt life lessons.

Looking back, The Princess Diaries wasn’t just a breakout role for Anne Hathaway, it was the beginning of one of Hollywood’s most successful careers. More than two decades later, Mia’s journey from ordinary teenager to confident young woman remains as charming and relatable as ever.

source_details.synopsis: The Princess Diaries is a 2001 American comedy film directed by Garry Marshall from a screenplay by Gina Wendkos. Produced by Walt Disney Pictures, it is based on Meg Cabot's 2000 novel of the same name and stars Anne Hathaway (in her film debut), Julie Andrews, Héctor Elizondo, Heather Matarazzo, Mandy Moore, Caroline Goodall, and Robert Schwartzman. In the film, shy American teenager Mia Thermopolis (Hathaway) learns she is crown princess of Genovia and receives tutelage from her estranged grandmother Clarisse Renaldi (Andrews), Genovia's Queen regent, as she decides whether to claim or renounce her title.
